newsitem.title: TOGO: Zaire crisis summit starts in Togo.
newsitem.headline: Zaire crisis summit starts in Togo.

text.p: A one-day summit on the Zaire crisis, called by the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), opened in Togo on Wednesday.

Thirteen African presidents, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and senior delegations from Zaire's embattled regime and advancing rebels were present when the summit opened at noon (1200 GMT), two hours behind schedule.

Leaders at the summit are pushing the warring parties to agree a ceasefire and commit themselves formally to negotiate. Laurent Kabila's rebels control a quarter of Zaire, five months after launching the revolt in the east.

The presidents at the opening ceremony with host Gnassingbe Eyadema of Togo were from Burundi, Cameroon, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Mauritania, Mozambique, Namibia, Sudan, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
South Africa, a key mediator on Zaire, was represented by Vice-President Thabo Mbeki.
